summary: Backend-only testing of Purchase History CRUD + Broadcast Filters. 17/18 tests passed; 1 skipped due to a real bug where add_purchase sets sold_count=None on the contact, breaking GET /api/contacts Pydantic validation (500 error). All 4 purchase CRUD endpoints and 4 broadcast preview filters verified working. Legacy migration test skipped pending the sold_count bug fix.

critical.issue: Sets 'sold_count: None' in $set during purchase creation. The Contact Pydantic model requires sold_count to be an integer, so GET /api/contacts returns 500 after a purchase is added. The line '$set: {"sold_count": None}' in add_purchase() causes a Pydantic ValidationError: 'Input should be a valid integer [type=int_type, input_value=None, input_type=NoneType]'
critical.fix: Remove 'sold_count: None' from the $set block in add_purchase(), or set it to a valid integer (e.g. incrementing the existing count). Alternatively, compute and set the correct count. Do NOT set it to None.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix add_purchase() in /app/backend/routers/contacts.py — remove '$set: {sold_count: None}' (line ~2215). This breaks GET /api/contacts returning 500 (Pydantic validation error) after any purchase is added to a contact.
After fixing sold_count, re-enable TestLegacyMigration::test_migration_for_contact_with_vehicle test (remove the 500 skip) to verify auto-migration of legacy vehicle/date_sold fields.
critical_code_review_comments: contacts.py add_purchase(): '$set: {"sold_count": None}' is intentionally a placeholder but breaks the Contact Pydantic schema. Either increment ($inc) sold_count by 1 or remove this line entirely.

broadcast.py purchase_category filter (lines 141-147): When purchase_title_contains is also set, the query builds a top-level 'purchase_history' key AND an '$or' with another $elemMatch. MongoDB may apply both but the compound $or/$elemMatch is untested for conflicts. In practice it worked for the test, but combining both filters simultaneously could be a latent edge case.

Auto-migration is read-only (does not write migrated entry back to DB), so every GET call will re-compute the migration. This is correct for safety but adds minor overhead per call for legacy contacts.
seed_data_creation: Created test contact with phone +15550000001 for user 69a0b7095fddcede09591667. Added several TEST_* purchases. These can be cleaned up manually.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Purchase CRUD endpoints all pass. The one real bug is add_purchase sets sold_count=None causing GET /api/contacts to 500. Fix: remove that $set line from add_purchase. After fix, re-run test_purchase_history.py and remove the 'skip on 500' guard in TestLegacyMigration to also verify legacy migration. Broadcast preview filters (purchase_title_contains, purchase_category, purchase_history_year) all working and verified. Response format is {success, count, sample[]} not a plain list.
rca_of_issue: RCA: In contacts.py add_purchase() at line ~2215, the $set includes '"sold_count": None' as a TODO placeholder for recounting. MongoDB stores null for sold_count. When GET /api/contacts serializes via the Contact Pydantic model, the field definition for sold_count expects int, causing ValidationError 500. Fix: remove the sold_count key from the $set, or use '$inc: {sold_count: 1}' instead.
